key_insight: The paper introduces CMA-AL, a six-level autonomy framework that standardizes how agentic AI can progress from scripted simulation workflows to self-extending materials discovery.
engineering_relevance: It gives computational materials engineers a common benchmark for assessing whether AI systems merely automate tasks or truly support autonomous scientific decision-making.
method: Define six autonomy levels: scripted executor, LLM-assisted operator, adaptive explorer, experiment-ready modeler, agentic digital twin, and self-extending intelligence.
Map emerging agentic systems onto the hierarchy to compare their scientific agency and maturity.
Use the framework to identify technical and scientific gaps needed for higher autonomy.
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a perspective paper that synthesizes emerging systems and proposes a taxonomy, but it does not report new experiments or quantitative benchmark results.
watch_item: The framework is conceptual, so practical adoption will depend on clear, reproducible criteria for assigning systems to each autonomy level.
paper_title: From Automated Simulation to Autonomous Discovery: A Hierarchical Framework for Agentic Computational Materials Science
